steps.title: Why Message Size Limits Exist
steps.text: Large messages cause memory pressure on brokers, increase network latency, slow replica synchronization, and can block consumer processing.

steps.title: Choosing a Strategy
steps.text: Under 1 MB: send directly. Between 1-10 MB: try compression first. Over 10 MB: use claim-check for batch processing or streaming for real-time needs.

steps.title: Compression Trade-offs
steps.text: LZ4 and Snappy are fast with low CPU cost. GZIP offers 4:1 ratio for bandwidth-constrained scenarios. ZSTD provides the best overall balance of speed and compression.

steps.title: Message Chunking
steps.text: Split oversized payloads into smaller chunks with sequence numbers and message IDs. Consumers reassemble chunks in order using the chunk header metadata.

steps.title: Claim-Check Pattern
steps.text: Store large payloads in external storage like S3 or Azure Blob, then send a lightweight reference message through Surgewave. Consumers fetch the full data on demand.
